# Incident Report — 2024-07-30 Network Capture Analysis

## Victim Host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **172.16.1.66** | Source of all beacon/C2 traffic; local LAN host (172.16.1.0/24) |
| MAC | **00:1e:64:ec:f3:08** | ARP replies and Ethernet source for 172.16.1.66 (confirmed against gateway 172.16.1.1 = 00:15:fa:50:6f:18 and DC 172.16.1.4 = 5c:f9:dd:8c:97:35) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-SKBR25F** | Kerberos CNameString (`DESKTOP-SKBR25F$`), NBNS name registration, DNS registration (`DESKTOP-SKBR25F.wiresharkworkshop.online` → 172.16.1.4/DDNS update), and repeated inside the malware's own beacon strings |
| Logged-in user | **ccollier** | Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString `ccollier` (frames to/from 172.16.1.4), and present in every C2 beacon payload |
| AD domain | wiresharkworkshop.online, DC = WIRESHARK-WS-DC (172.16.1.4) | LDAP/CLDAP/Kerberos/DRSUAPI traffic — benign domain-join context |

## Malware Family
**STRRAT** (Java-based RAT/backdoor, known for fake-ransomware `.crimson` extension behavior and credential-stealing/keylogging capability).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** No separate IDS/Suricata alert file was present in the evidence directory, but the malware's own C2 protocol banner literally contains the family name in plaintext on the wire:

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender|<base64 active-window-title>|1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<idle time>
```

This is the STRRAT client "ping" heartbeat format (client ID `1BE8292C`), sent every 5 seconds over a raw TCP socket (no TLS, no HTTP framing) — each ping is preceded by a length-prefix packet (`136\r\n\r\n`, `137\r\n\r\n`, etc.) then the pipe-delimited status line, base64-encoding the victim's currently focused window title (decoded values observed: "Documents", "Home", "Pictures", "Program Manager", "Fanad Head Lighthouse - Paint", "pounds-formula [Compatibility Mode] - PowerPoint") — consistent with STRRAT's active-window/keylogging telemetry.

## Indicators of Compromise (grounded in capture)

| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C2 endpoint | **141.98.10.79:12132** | TCP stream 172.16.1.66:49754 ↔ 141.98.10.79:12132, first SYN at t=76.99s, persists to end of capture (t=585.66s) at ~5s beacon interval; plaintext STRRAT ping payloads (see above) carried over this socket, no DNS lookup preceded it (hardcoded C2 IP) |
| Behavioral artifact | STRRAT client ID `1BE8292C` | Constant across all ~100+ beacon payloads on the C2 socket |

No additional malicious domains, URLs, or transferred/dropped files could be grounded in this capture: the only HTTP traffic in the trace is a benign Microsoft NCSI connectivity check (`www.msftconnecttest.com/connecttest.txt`) and a plaintext lookup of `ip-api.com/json/` (208.95.112.1) using an old spoofed Chrome/73 user agent — likely the malware or a companion component performing a geolocation/IP check (consistent with the `US:United States` field in the STRRAT beacon), but the request body itself is standard IP-API JSON, not malicious content, so it's listed as supporting context rather than a hard IOC. No jar/executable transfer, no additional TLS SNI to non-Microsoft/non-benign infrastructure, and no delivery-chain (initial infection vector) traffic appear in this capture — the STRRAT beacon is already active at the start of the trace, meaning the initial compromise predates this pcap.

## Benign Context (not IOCs)
- All AD/domain traffic (LDAP, CLDAP, Kerberos, DRSUAPI, SAMR, NBNS/NBDGM/browser) to DC 172.16.1.4 — normal Windows domain operation.
- All Microsoft telemetry/services traffic (mobile.events.data.microsoft.com, go.microsoft.com, officeclient/odc.officeapps.live.com, login.microsoftonline.com, autodiscover, msn.com/bing.com family, client.wns.windows.com, settings-win.data.microsoft.com, etc.) — standard Windows 11 / Office background noise.
- github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com, repo1.maven.org, javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com — developer tooling downloads (Java/Maven ecosystem), no malicious payload observed in this traffic.
- ip-api.com/json/ lookup — flagged above as possibly malware-related but the transaction itself is standard IP geolocation API usage.

## Incident Summary
The Windows 11 workstation **DESKTOP-SKBR25F** (172.16.1.66, MAC 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08), logged in as domain user **ccollier**, was actively compromised by **STRRAT** for the full 585-second duration of this capture. The malware beaconed every ~5 seconds in plaintext to its C2 server at **141.98.10.79:12132**, self-identifying its family name, a persistent client ID (`1BE8292C`), host/user details, and the victim's active window title (keylogger/screen-monitoring telemetry) in each check-in. The initial infection vector is not present in this capture — the C2 channel is already established at trace start — so delivery-chain artifacts (dropper file, lure URL, initial download) could not be recovered from this evidence.
